answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-decay reputation: an agent must lock a deposit before it can transact, and trust accrues only from verified completed work, never from self-assertion. New identities start at zero, so spawning clones costs real capital without instant credibility. Imagine a knoll at dusk where each agent carries a lantern: the light shows who has actually delivered, while umber shadows hide nothing - cheap copies stay dim, untrusted, and any proven fraud slashes the deposit, making mass imitation unprofitable.
